lean.fidelity_note: For the smooth Euler limit of the common construction, the formal statement gives both printed conclusions: one finite bound for the velocity throughout $[0,T_\infty)$ and the full limit $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$. It additionally supplies fixed real constants $c>0,C$ and an index $J$ such that, for every $j\ge J$ and every $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$. This bound is for the limiting solution, whereas (8.2) bounds the approximation and uses the older-gradient term $\lambda_{j-2}^9$. The constants are independent of the late index and time. The velocity norm is the essential supremum on the unit cell. The stronger interval estimate, together with crossing-duration bounds, supplies the direct integral argument in the formal Corollary 8.3; a divergent pointwise limit alone would not suffice.

statements.markdown: **Proposition 8.2.** The solution has bounded velocity on $[0,T_\infty)$, and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\longrightarrow\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$.
statements.section: 8.2 Velocity, central vorticity and the maximal time
